For the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations linearized around a monotonic shear flow $(U(y),0)$ with background density $\rho_0(y)$, the relevant spectral object is the **distorted Rayleigh operator**, which contains terms involving $U''$ and $\rho_0'/\rho_0$. 

Because the base profiles depend only on the transverse variable $y\in[0,1]$, their regularity is governed by **one-dimensional Sobolev embedding**:
- To make classical sense of $U''$ (and to ensure the distorted Rayleigh operator has the standard Fredholm / limiting-absorption properties needed for rigidity), one needs $U\in C^2$, which in 1D corresponds exactly to $H^{5/2+\tau}$ for any $\tau>0$. Thus the critical velocity exponent is $s_v=\frac52$.
- To control the density-gradient terms in the generalized Rayleigh equation, one needs $\rho_0\in C^1$, which in 1D corresponds to $H^{3/2+\tau}$. Thus the critical density exponent is $s_\rho=\frac32$.

Below these thresholds ($H^{s_v-\tau}$ and $H^{s_\rho-\tau}$) the coefficients are too rough to preclude singular eigenfunctions, and nontrivial traveling waves can indeed be constructed. Above them ($H^{s_v+\tau}$ and $H^{s_\rho+\tau}$), provided the distorted Rayleigh operator admits no eigenvalues or embedded eigenvalues, such traveling waves are ruled out.

Hence
$$s_v+s_\rho=\frac52+\frac32=4.$$

\boxed{4}
